alex.h: Hey support — getting 401 invalid_api_key on hosted endpoint. Quick curl:
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "x-api-key: 🔐abcd1234efgh5678" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"hi"}'
```

Response: {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key"}}

maria_support: thanks — can you paste the raw header value (no redaction) inside triple backticks? also, did you rotate keys recently or pull from a secret manager?

alex.h: i regenerated yesterday. pasting raw header (redacting middle for public):
`🔐abcd1234efgh5678`

jay_sre: hunch — looks like a leading emoji got copied into the key. our API keys are ASCII-only. can you check the raw bytes to confirm? e.g.:
```bash
printf '%s' '🔐abcd1234efgh5678' | xxd
```

alex.h: result i see:
`00000000: f09f 9490 6162 6364 3132 3334 6566 6768  ....abcd1234efgh`

maria_support: yup that confirms it — the `f0 9f 94 90` bytes are the emoji (🔐). when copying from Slack or docs that use inline emoji, the emoji can become prepended to the copied string. the token no longer matches our expected pattern so we return invalid_api_key.

maria_support: solution paths:
- easiest: rotate/regenerate a new key and update your env — make sure to paste into a plain text editor and verify there are no leading non-ASCII chars.
- if you need a quick fix: run `tr -cd '\11\12\15\40-\176' <keyfile >cleankey` to strip non-ASCII, but rotating is safer.

alex.h: rotated to a new key and tested — 200 OK now. thanks for the fast triage! :tada:

deploy-bot: Key rotation completed for account acct-1234 (rotated by alex.h) — audit id audit-7890

maria_support: adding a docs note to warn about emoji/hidden chars when copying keys. closing this thread unless you want us to keep it open.

alex.h: all good, closing from my side too. thank you!
